blocks.html: Six services, each with a written scope

Every project starts with a scope document: what is delivered, what is not, and what you need to supply. If you are unsure where to start, the service finder suggests one in six questions. Out of these same projects we also write articles on website cost, scope and sales.

items:
Website building

A website with structure: modeled, built, and handed over with documentation, so it keeps working after launch day.

Not a fit if you only want a ready-made template in your brand colours.

About website building

UI/UX design

Interfaces decided by user tasks and evidence, delivered as a system developers can actually build from.

Not a fit if you only need a few screens to show investors.

About UI/UX design

Business model design

A model you can test: assumptions, revenue logic, and kill/continue criteria, not just a convincing pitch deck.

Not a fit if you need a financial forecast or investment advice.

About business model design

Documentation

Documents the next maintainer can use, with a named audience, format, and update rule.

Not a fit if the document only needs to exist in a folder.

About documentation

Penetration testing

A manual, scoped test with a CVSS-scored report and a retest: proof of what was tested, and what was not.

Not a fit without written authorisation from the system owner, or if you want a "fully secure" certificate.

About penetration testing

Marketing and content

Video, text, and SEO built from the same structure as the product, so content explains the work instead of decorating it.

Not a fit if you want a promised Google ranking.

About marketing and content

blocks.html: Five steps, each with a named input and output

items: Discover: goal, audience, and success are defined before any design starts.
Plan: structure, pages or features, and priorities are agreed up front.
Design: a direction you see and react to early, not a finished site revealed at the end.
Build: clean, component-based code, with performance and accessibility from the start and documentation as we go.
Launch and care: release, a handover walkthrough, and a retest or revision under that service's rule.

blocks.html: Neither tool sends your answers anywhere.

blocks.a_html:
How is price decided?

Before any price, we have a scoping conversation. After it, we send a written proposal with a fixed price for a defined scope.

How long does it take?

It depends on the scope and on content readiness. We write the schedule into the proposal as an estimate, not a guarantee.

blocks.q: What if my content is not ready?
blocks.a_html:
What if my content is not ready?

That is fine, as long as we know from the start. Content readiness is one of the effort-band factors and is written into the scope.

What happens after delivery?

We hold a handover walkthrough and give you the handover documentation, so you or the next team can maintain the work. Each service's revision or retest rule is written into that service's scope.

blocks.q: Who owns the site, code, domain, and content?
blocks.a_html:
Who owns the site, code, domain, and content?

You do. The source code, domain, hosting account and content are handed over in your name.

Can you guarantee SEO rankings?

No. Nobody can honestly guarantee a specific Google ranking. What we can promise is structure, speed and content readiness for search.
